course: Daily Pig Sales: Batch Farrowing System

lessons.title: Farrowing Supervision
lessons.body: Farrowing supervision means being present when the sow gives birth. Most piglets die during the first 3 days, so your presence can save many lives. Start by preparing a clean, dry farrowing pen with a heat lamp or heat box for the piglets. The sow needs a quiet, dark area with no drafts. Write down the expected farrowing date (114 days after mating) and check the sow every 4 hours starting 2 days before. When she starts nesting, restless, and her udder swells, she will farrow within 12-24 hours. Stay nearby. As each piglet is born, tear the sac if it covers the face, wipe mucus from the nose and mouth with a clean cloth, and dry the piglet with a towel or dry straw. Tie the umbilical cord with a clean string about 2 cm from the belly and cut it with disinfected scissors. Dip the stump in iodine. Put the piglet under the heat lamp or in a warm box. Make sure it gets colostrum within 30 minutes. If a piglet is born without breathing, rub its chest vigorously and hold it upside down for a few seconds. If the sow is in distress or no piglet comes after 30 minutes of straining, call a vet. Count the placentas; there should be one per piglet. Keep a record of births, deaths, and any problems. Supervised farrowing can reduce stillbirths and crushing. In Africa, where many farmers cannot afford constant vet care, simple supervision by the farmer is the cheapest way to save piglets. Stay calm, keep the area clean, and act quickly.

lessons.title: Colostrum in the First 6 Hours
lessons.body: Colostrum is the first milk a sow produces. It is thick, yellowish, and rich in antibodies that protect piglets from disease. Piglets are born with no immunity, so they must drink colostrum within the first 6 hours of life. After 6 hours, their gut can no longer absorb the antibodies. The first 30 minutes are best. Make sure every piglet gets colostrum. If a piglet is weak, hold it to a teat and squeeze a few drops into its mouth. The best teats are the front ones, which give more milk. If a sow has more piglets than teats, rotate the smaller piglets to the front and the stronger ones to the back. If a sow dies or has no milk, use colostrum from another sow that farrowed within 24 hours, or use a commercial colostrum replacer. In Africa, you can also use cow colostrum as a last resort, but pig colostrum is best. Never give water or glucose before colostrum; it can damage the gut. Keep the piglets warm while they suckle. A cold piglet will not suckle. If a piglet has not suckled within 2 hours, assist it. Check that the sow has enough teats; if not, consider cross-fostering to another sow that farrowed at the same time. Cross-fostering works best within 24 hours. Always wash your hands before handling piglets. After the first 6 hours, piglets can drink regular milk. But colostrum is the foundation of their health. Without it, they will likely die from diarrhea or pneumonia. So be there at farrowing and make sure every piglet gets its share.

lessons.title: Keeping Piglets Warm
lessons.body: Newborn piglets cannot control their body temperature. They need a warm, dry place away from the sow. The ideal temperature for a newborn piglet is 32-35Â°C. For a 3-week-old piglet, 24-28Â°C is fine. If piglets are cold, they huddle, shiver, and refuse to suckle. They can die within hours. In Africa, many farmers use a heat lamp (infrared bulb) hung 45-60 cm above the floor. A 100-watt bulb is enough for a small pen. If you have no electricity, use a heat box: a wooden box with a lid and a small entrance, filled with dry straw. The piglets' body heat warms the box. You can also use a charcoal stove, but keep it outside the pen to avoid fumes. Another option is a hot water bottle wrapped in a towel. Place the heat source in a corner, away from the sow. The piglets will learn to go there. Bedding must be dry and clean. Wet bedding draws heat away. Use dry straw, wood shavings, or shredded paper. Change it daily. Avoid drafts. Fix holes in walls or use curtains. In hot climates, piglets may need cooling during the day, but nights can be cold. Monitor piglets: if they are spread out and panting, it's too hot; if they are piled up and shivering, it's too cold. Adjust the heat lamp height or add more bedding. A simple thermometer helps. Keep the farrowing pen at 20Â°C for the sow, but provide a warmer microclimate for piglets. This reduces crushing because piglets will not seek warmth under the sow. Warm piglets are active, suckle well, and grow faster. So invest in a heat source; it pays back in saved piglets.

lessons.title: Iron Injection and Iron Deficiency
lessons.body: Piglets are born with very little iron. Sow's milk has almost no iron. Without extra iron, piglets become anemic: their skin looks pale, they breathe fast, and they grow slowly. Anemia can kill them. In nature, piglets get iron from soil, but in confinement, you must inject iron. Give 200 mg of iron dextran injection to each piglet at 3 days of age. Use a 1 ml syringe with a 20-gauge needle. Inject into the neck muscle, behind the ear, or into the ham. Clean the skin with alcohol first. Do not inject into the same spot twice; rotate sides. If you cannot get iron dextran, some farmers use iron paste or iron-rich soil, but injection is best. In Africa, iron dextran is available from agrovets. Store it in a cool, dark place. Do not use expired product. If piglets are very pale at birth, give iron at 1 day old. Repeat if needed at 2 weeks. Signs of iron deficiency include pale gums, rough hair, and poor weight gain. If you see these, inject iron immediately. Also, ensure piglets have access to clean soil or a mineral block after 1 week. Some farmers give iron via the sow's feed, but that does not pass enough to piglets. So injection is necessary. Keep records of dates and doses. A simple notebook works. Iron injection is quick and cheap. One bottle of iron dextran treats many piglets. It prevents anemia and helps piglets survive to weaning. So do not skip it.

lessons.title: Castration and Tail Docking
lessons.body: Castration and tail docking are done to reduce boar taint and tail biting. Castrate male piglets at 3-7 days old. At this age, they are small and heal fast. Use a sharp, clean scalpel or a castration knife. Wash your hands and the piglet's scrotum with soap and water. Hold the piglet upside down by the hind legs. Make a small cut in the scrotum, push out the testicle, and pull it out with a gentle twist. Cut the cord. Repeat on the other side. Apply iodine to the wounds. Do not use a knife that is rusty. Do not castrate sick or weak piglets. If you are not confident, get a vet or experienced farmer to show you. Tail docking: cut the tail 2-3 cm from the base with clean scissors or a hot iron. This prevents tail biting later. Do it at the same time as castration. Use a hot iron to cauterize and reduce bleeding. After docking, apply iodine. Keep piglets in a clean, dry pen. Watch for bleeding or infection. If a piglet bleeds a lot, press a clean cloth on the wound. In Africa, some farmers use rubber rings for castration, but they are not recommended because they cause pain and tetanus risk. Always use sterile tools. Do not castrate after 2 weeks; it is more stressful. If you sell piglets for meat, castration is important because uncastrated males have a strong smell. Tail docking reduces injuries from biting. Both are quick if done correctly. So learn the technique and do it early.

lessons.title: Reducing Crushing Deaths
lessons.body: Crushing is the biggest killer of piglets before weaning. The sow accidentally lies on them. To reduce crushing, you need to change the pen and the sow's behavior. First, provide a safe creep area for piglets: a corner with a heat lamp and bedding, blocked off by a low wall so the sow cannot enter. Piglets will learn to sleep there. Second, keep the pen warm for piglets but cool for the sow. If the sow is too hot, she will lie spread out and may crush piglets. Use a heat lamp only over the creep area, not the whole pen. Third, handle the sow gently. A stressed sow is more likely to lie down suddenly. Fourth, install anti-crushing rails: a horizontal bar 20-25 cm from the floor along the walls. When the sow lies down, the rail gives piglets a gap to escape. Fifth, supervise farrowing and the first 3 days. When the sow is about to lie down, watch her. If a piglet is under her, move it. Sixth, keep the floor dry and non-slip. Wet floors cause sows to slip and fall on piglets. Seventh, feed the sow in a trough away from the creep area. Eighth, if a sow is known to crush piglets, consider using a farrowing crate, but crates are expensive and can stress the sow. In Africa, simple pens with a creep area and rails work well. Also, ensure piglets are not too cold; cold piglets huddle near the sow and get crushed. So warmth is key. Check pens every few hours, especially at night. Remove dead piglets immediately. With these steps, you can cut crushing deaths by half.

quiz.q: What is the ideal temperature for a newborn piglet?
quiz.explanation: Newborn piglets cannot regulate their body temperature and need 32-35Â°C.

quiz.q: How soon after birth should a piglet receive colostrum?
quiz.explanation: The gut can only absorb antibodies from colostrum for about 6 hours after birth.

quiz.q: What is the main purpose of iron injection in piglets?
quiz.explanation: Piglets are born with low iron and sow's milk is iron-poor, so injection prevents anemia.

quiz.q: At what age is castration recommended for piglets?
quiz.explanation: Castration at 3-7 days is less stressful and heals faster.

quiz.q: Which of these helps reduce crushing deaths?
options: A) Keeping the pen hot for the sow
B) Providing a creep area for piglets
C) Feeding the sow in the creep area
quiz.explanation: A creep area gives piglets a safe place away from the sow.

quiz.q: What should you do first when a piglet is born?
options: B) Wipe the nose and mouth
quiz.explanation: Clearing the airway helps the piglet breathe immediately.

quiz.q: How much iron dextran is given to a piglet?
quiz.explanation: The standard dose is 200 mg of iron dextran per piglet.

quiz.q: What is a sign of iron deficiency in piglets?
quiz.explanation: Anemia causes pale skin and gums due to low red blood cells.

quiz.q: Why is tail docking done?
options: D) To make piglets easier to handle
quiz.explanation: Tail docking reduces tail biting among pigs.

quiz.q: What is the best way to warm piglets without electricity?
options: A) Use a charcoal stove inside the pen
B) Use a heat box with dry straw
C) Use a hot water bottle uncovered
D) Cover them with a wet cloth
quiz.explanation: A heat box with dry straw traps body heat and is safe.

quiz.q: How often should you check the sow during farrowing?
quiz.explanation: Frequent checks allow you to assist if problems arise.

quiz.q: What is colostrum?
quiz.explanation: Colostrum is the first milk produced by the sow, rich in antibodies.

quiz.q: What should you do if a piglet is born not breathing?
options: A) Rub its chest and hold upside down
C) Put it under the heat lamp
quiz.explanation: Rubbing the chest and clearing fluids can stimulate breathing.

quiz.q: Which teats give more milk?
quiz.explanation: Front teats have more milk, so smaller piglets should be put there.

quiz.q: What is cross-fostering?
options: A) Moving piglets to another sow
quiz.explanation: Cross-fostering means giving piglets to another lactating sow.

quiz.q: What is an anti-crushing rail?
options: A) A bar along the wall to protect piglets
B) A fence around the creep area
quiz.explanation: The rail creates a gap so piglets can escape when the sow lies down.

quiz.q: When should you castrate a piglet?
quiz.explanation: Early castration is less stressful and heals faster.

quiz.q: What should you apply to the umbilical stump after cutting?
quiz.explanation: Iodine disinfects the stump and prevents infection.

quiz.q: Why is it important to keep piglets warm?
quiz.explanation: Warm piglets are active and will suckle; cold piglets refuse to suckle.

quiz.q: What is the ideal temperature for a 3-week-old piglet?
quiz.explanation: As piglets grow, their temperature needs decrease to 24-28Â°C.

quiz.q: What is a sign that piglets are too cold?
options: A) They are spread out and panting
B) They are piled up and shivering
quiz.explanation: Huddling and shivering indicate cold stress.

quiz.q: How often should you change bedding in the farrowing pen?
quiz.explanation: Daily changing keeps bedding dry and reduces disease.

quiz.q: What is the main cause of piglet deaths before weaning?
quiz.explanation: Crushing is the leading cause of pre-weaning mortality.

quiz.q: What should you do if a sow has more piglets than teats?
options: A) Rotate piglets to front teats
quiz.explanation: Rotating ensures all piglets get access to the richer front teats.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of tail docking?
options: D) To make piglets easier to handle
quiz.explanation: Tail docking reduces tail biting among pigs.

quiz.q: What should you use to cut the umbilical cord?
quiz.explanation: Clean scissors prevent infection.

quiz.q: What is the best time to give iron injection?
quiz.explanation: Iron injection is recommended at 3 days of age.

quiz.q: What is a creep area?
options: A) A warm, safe area for piglets
B) A feeding area for the sow
C) A place to castrate piglets
quiz.explanation: A creep area is a heated, protected zone for piglets.

quiz.q: What should you do if a piglet is bleeding after castration?
options: A) Apply pressure with a clean cloth
D) Put it under heat lamp
quiz.explanation: Pressure helps stop bleeding.

quiz.q: Why is colostrum important?
quiz.explanation: Colostrum is rich in antibodies that protect against disease.
